[element-doc-ref]
=== `<doc-ref>` Document Reference Designation

A pre-constructed, formatted reference to the standard that is used for display purposes (such as online display or assembling PDF), particularly when an editorial variant of the designation is needed for rendering.

#### Usage/Remarks
A typical <<element-doc-ref,`<doc-ref>`>> element includes the standard’s designator and other information such as the language of the standard, e.g., “`ISO 2560:2009(en)`”. While it would usually be possible to construct the <<element-doc-ref,`<doc-ref>`>> from the content of other metadata elements, the pre-combined <<element-doc-ref,`<doc-ref>`>> form provides a convenience for rendering, without resorting to a transform or hardcoding editorial rules.

#### Related Elements

Contrast this with the metadata element <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>>, which gives a reference form of identifier for a standard, typically the designator. In some cases, a <<element-doc-ref,`<doc-ref>`>> will contain the same content as one of the <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>>s; in other cases <<element-doc-ref,`<doc-ref>`>> may be a slight variant. (Note that there can be several <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>>s, such as dated and undated forms, distinguished by the <<attribute-type,`@type`>> attribute.)

 ...

 <std-ref type="dated">ISO 2560:2009</std-ref>
 <doc-ref>ISO 2560:2009(en)</doc-ref>
 <release-date iso-8601-date="2009-05-30" 
   date-type="published">2009-05-30</release-date>
 ...  
</iso-meta>
...
